findings.title: The formal scanner contract matrix does not require a production positive and safe-negative for every declared binary magic
findings.failure_condition: One declared non-MZ magic loses both of its production positive and safe-negative cases while the binary oracle and scanner implementation still declare that magic.
findings.reproducible_read_only_check: In an A7 reviewer-temp copy, remove one non-MZ magic pair from scanner-production-case-manifest.json, then run the contract equality fixture and production scanner runner against that copy.
findings.observed: Removing the JPEG pair left CASE-54 PASS and produced a green 70/70 production scanner run. Direct contract checks returned no violation when the ELF, ZIP, PDF, SQLITE, PGDMP, OLE, PNG, or JPEG pair was removed. Removing MZ was rejected because the single KNOWN_BINARY_MAGIC_DETECTED matrix row names only the MZ pair.
findings.expected: The contract bundle must be invalid unless every one of the nine oracle signatures has an exact production entrypoint, positive case, and safe-negative case; the production runner must reject any case-set reduction from the trusted 72-case identity.
findings.impact: The filed formal oracle can stay fully green after losing the regression proof for eight declared magic signatures. This directly contradicts the R7 claim that missing per-magic matrix coverage fails and leaves the A5/A6 scanner-oracle trust boundary incomplete.
required_resolution: Derive required per-magic production case IDs from scanner-binary-oracle.yaml or encode all nine signature pairs explicitly in the implementation matrix.
Validate exact production case identity, count, uniqueness, mode, finding class, and formal entrypoint before accepting the scanner contract bundle.
Add removal mutations for every magic positive and safe-negative pair and require both CASE-54 and the production runner to fail on any missing pair.
findings.remaining_risk: Until the formal oracle enforces exact per-magic coverage, a future governance change can silently narrow binary regression evidence while retaining green authoritative results.

reproducible_exploit_retest.observed: Schema and semantic validation rejected forged version, all four scanner bundle hashes, manifest, included/scanned sets, counts, claims, finding registry use, and payload. Both candidate generation and Task validation fail closed, and a consistent nonzero-finding report cannot form a candidate.

closure_dispositions.remaining_risk: Bootstrap report and validator code remain mutable workspace artifacts and producer identity remains procedural; those declared limitations do not reproduce the closed report-binding bypass.

reproducible_exploit_retest.observed: Current binary config equality checks reject registry, entropy, and binary-oracle drift, and extension-magic-mismatch is no longer claimed. However, removing any non-MZ magic positive/safe-negative production pair is accepted by validateDeclaredScanContract; a JPEG reduction leaves CASE-54 and a 70/70 production run green.

closure_dispositions.remaining_risk: The exact current candidate contains all nine pairs, but its formal regression boundary does not prove those pairs are mandatory and therefore can remain green after evidence coverage is removed.

reproducible_exploit_retest.observed: The current 72-case suite executes every declared class and all nine magics, but the filed oracle still does not enforce the full declared per-magic matrix: eight magic pairs can be removed without failing contract equality or the reduced production run.

closure_dispositions.remaining_risk: A later regression can remove advertised binary coverage while the authoritative suite reports all remaining cases green, which is the original filed-oracle failure mode.

candidate_review_gate_recommendation.reason: A6-SEC-HIGH-002 and A5-SEC-HIGH-002 remain NOT_CLOSED because the formal binary oracle does not enforce every declared magic positive/safe-negative pair.

residual_risks: All bootstrap validators, reports, manifests, and review identities are mutable workspace artifacts with INTERNAL_CONSISTENCY_ONLY assurance and no Git trust anchor.
The scanner is bounded deterministic detection for the exact 92-file manifest, not DLP, repository-global scanning, or proof that all sensitive data is absent.
Unknown, encrypted, compressed, fragmented, split, or beyond-contract multiply encoded content remains outside the declared scanner boundary.
Current manifest paths had no reparse points and resolved inside the product root, but safeExistingPath followed by later file reads does not provide atomic TOCTOU protection.
Test runners use child processes and temporary copied workspaces for isolation checks; this is not an operating-system sandbox or proof against parent-process override.
No product, service, database, seed, migration, external executable isolation, or Railway business behavior was inspected or executed.
conclusion: A6-SEC-HIGH-001 is CLOSED: scanner v5 report and candidate bindings fail closed for the specified forged fields and nonzero findings. A6-SEC-HIGH-002 and A5-SEC-HIGH-002 are NOT_CLOSED: although the exact current candidate has 72 passing production cases, the formal contract matrix requires only the MZ magic pair and permits the other eight per-magic positive/safe-negative pairs to be removed while CASE-54 and the reduced production suite remain green. The A7 Security outcome is BLOCKER; Bootstrap Candidate Review remains NO-GO, Bootstrap Human Commit remains NO-GO, both steady-state gates remain DISABLED, Migration 320 remains NO-GO, and Session B remains unauthorized.
